Treat any single number as approximate.

text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Green Bay's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Green Bay has set 32 standing record lows, far fewer than the 70 that chance alone would give, and 109 record highs, far more than the 70 that chance alone would give. The 2020s hold the most record highs of any decade (49). Green Bay's all-time high is 104°F, on July 13, 1936.
text.t_chg: Green Bay's nights have warmed since 1986. Its days warmed over the long run.
text.p_chg: Across 139 complete years: Green Bay's average low shows no clear change: +0.04°F per decade, a range (−0.04 to +0.12) that includes zero. Green Bay's average high has risen +0.24°F per decade (95% range +0.17 to +0.31), about +3.3°F since 1887. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +0.75°F per decade (95% range +0.28 to +1.23) and highs show no clear change. The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 2 of 12 months; September fell. Highs rose in 9 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Green Bay's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.17 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 31.6 inches a year. The wettest year was 2019 (48.63 in); the driest, 1930 (16.31 in).
